existing.description: The International Visegrad Fund's Visegrad Scholarship Programme supports master's and post-master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe, awarded for a period of 1 or 2 semesters; within the In-Coming scheme, master's applicants can be awarded 1- to 4-semester scholarships. It is open to citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine, and all applicants must have completed at least four semesters of university studies. Because it is a mobility scholarship, the host country varies with the chosen institution rather than being a single destination. The Fund's own site shows the next application round opening on 1 January 2027; no closing date for that round is published yet, and the funding amounts are not stated on the pages read, so funding_type and funding_amount are left unresolved rather than guessed.
eligibility: Citizenship of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia or Ukraine
Completion of at least four semesters of university studies
Master's or post-master's level of study or research
Placement at an institution in Central and Eastern Europe for 1 or 2 semesters; master's applicants within the In-Coming scheme may be awarded 1 to 4 semesters
Cannot apply for a scholarship at an institution in the applicant's own country of citizenship or residence, as the scheme funds mobility
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine may apply. existing.selection_notes: The Fund describes mobility, whether for study or research, as "a central part of our aim to foster creativity and promote understanding between people across borders", and it looks for "individuals pursuing innovative ideas in science and education wishing to engage in conversation on development and cooperation in Visegrad region". Selection therefore favours academically substantive study or research proposals with a regional development dimension.
existing.best_fit: Master's and post-master's students and researchers from the Western Balkans and Eastern Partnership countries who have completed at least four semesters and can secure a placement at a Central and Eastern European institution.
